business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Marine Outboard Engines and Compact Generators

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Roman-Germanic tradition with mandatory notarial intervention for company formation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-Argentina Bilateral Investment Treaty on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (1992)
Spain-Mexico Bilateral Investment Treaty on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (1995)
EU-Colombia-Peru Trade Agreement (2013), applicable to Spain
Spain-China Double Taxation Agreement on Income and Capital (1992), as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; and Circular 1/2021 of the SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Existencia Legal) of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or equivalent authority of shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certification pursuant to the Convention abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder General) in favor of the Spanish incorporation representative or agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity card of each director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or civil registry office of the jurisdiction of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification followed by Hague Apostille certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution maintaining the account for the transferring shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certification or consular legalization in non-Hague counterpart jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs must be screened before incorporation against: (i) SEPBLAC domestic politically exposed person (PEP) indicators; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (CFSP); (iv) US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list for any USD-denominated Swift_LC or TT_Wire payment rails; and (v) Spanish Agencia Tributaria criminal/tax enforcement and insolvency disqualification records. Screening results must be retained in a written AML/CFT file for at least ten years and reported to SEPBLAC under a designated compliance officer when any positive or risk-flag occurs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — online portal for Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article 407 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, the social denomination must be expressed in Spanish or transliterated into Spanish orthography when using foreign expressions. The name must be unique and not confusingly similar to any existing Spanish registered company or internationally protected trademark; accented or diacritical signs are normalized to Spanish script for registry indexing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon an adverse name-denomination decision, the applicant or acting notary may file the Certificación Negativa denial and file a ministerial-grade administrative appeal (Recurso de Alzada) before the Registro Mercantil Central within one month of notification under Ley 39/2015, of 1 October, of Common Administrative Procedure. Alternatively, a corrected application may be made with alternative denominations. Where rejection is grounded on prior trademark rights, the applicant may obtain an official trademark search report and request reconsideration before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. A virtual-office service providing a physical mailbox, reception, and legal notification address is acceptable for the technical registered-office requirement during incorporation. However, for ISIC 2811 manufacture of marine outboard engines, an industrial production site or verifiable operational location will be required to evidence commercial substance and effective management; a purely desk-based virtual address will attract heightened review by the Agencia Tributaria and SEPBLAC and may be deemed inadequate for VAT and transfer-pricing purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-elevated for manufacturing entities — estimated 40% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by Agencia Tributaria, SEPBLAC, or Inspección de Trabajo y Seguridad Social (ITSS) within the first three fiscal years where no physical production facility is demonstrable; probability reduces below 15% when a conventional industrial premises is registered, staffed, and compliant with environmental and occupational safety regulations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff per name-certificate application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of articles of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Selected Notary Public in the jurisdiction of registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff scale under Spanish Notaries Regulations, inclusive of tax on documented legal acts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registry inscription (Inscripción en el Registro Mercantil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff based on stated share capital and legal acts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille bundle for foreign corporate and personal documents (3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Apostille authority in country of origin (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs or equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille statutory fee, prevailing international market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of non-Spanish corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator / Oficina de Interpretación de Lenguas (OIL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per word/page (approx. EUR 20–25 per page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO due diligence and PEP/sanctions screening report by external counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External law firm retained by the shareholder
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee professional services benchmark in Madrid/Valencia corporate practice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office service (mailbox and administrative address), 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider or business center
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for registered office mailbox and notification forwarding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional Spanish tax identification number application (NIF provisional)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; administrative processing time only

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account setup and share-capital deposit confirmation letter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish credit institution selected for the SL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee schedule for company account opening, commonly waived under commercial packages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency for name-certificate renewal and authorized notarial copy (copia autorizada)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory renewal tariff plus notarial copy fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 20–23, 31–33, 210–212, and 233–234; Law 14/2013 governs the CIRCE and DUE electronic formation channel.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The Mercantile Registry for the province in which the registered office is located (Registro Mercantil Provincial), coordinated nationally by the College of Registrars of Spain.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), filed for registration in the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry; the deed must include the articles of association and required incorporation particulars.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An SL may be incorporated with stated share capital of at least EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until share capital plus legal reserve reaches EUR 3,000, the company must allocate at least 20% of annual profit to legal reserve; on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may be jointly and severally liable for the shortfall up to EUR 3,000. No statutory escrow account is required. Notarial and Mercantile Registry charges are separately payable under applicable tariffs; there is no single fixed central state filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscriptions for the shares set out in the notarized deed of incorporation and record that the subscribed capital has been fully paid as required by law. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full address], Spain, subject to registration of that address in the deed and the Mercantile Registry. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed [sole director / joint directors / board members], and that [name] be appointed managing director, if applicable, with the authority stated in the articles and appointment instrument. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to obtain the Company’s tax identification number, complete registration formalities, open bank accounts, and submit required regulatory notifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its official online name-reservation service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a negative name certificate listing up to five proposed names in order of preference. Use the exact proposed name, including the required SL designation, in the incorporation deed. The certificate is time-limited; coordinate deed execution and filing within its validity period.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application and applicable fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If all proposed names are unavailable or rejected, submit additional distinctive names and obtain a new certificate before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain founder tax identifiers and prepare foreign-founder documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) for tax identification; Spanish consulate, competent foreign authority, and Spanish notary for legalization or notarization as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Spanish NIF for each founder and director who requires one. Non-resident individuals generally require an NIE; non-resident legal entities require a Spanish NIF and evidence of existence, authority, and ownership. Have foreign public documents apostilled or legalized as applicable and translated into Spanish by a sworn translator. Confirm the notary’s documentary and beneficial-owner requirements before execution.
required_dossiers: NIE or NIF certificates, as applicable
For corporate founders: current registry extract or certificate of good standing, constitutional documents, and evidence of signatory authority
Apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translations, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct identification discrepancies, obtain missing tax identifiers, and provide replacement legalized, translated, or certified documents. Request a notarial deficiency list before rescheduling execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Set share capital, governance, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating notary public (notario); AEAT for any required pre-incorporation NIF procedure.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine the share capital, shareholder allocations, management structure, powers, registered office, corporate purpose, and financial year. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid. The notary may accept a bank certificate evidencing deposit or the founders’ joint and several declaration of contribution under the Companies Act; no statutory escrow account is prescribed. Ensure the corporate purpose accurately covers the planned manufacturing activity.
required_dossiers: Founder and director identification and tax numbers
Evidence of cash contribution or legally compliant founder declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the articles, contribution evidence, or corporate purpose to address the notary’s objections; obtain corrected name or identification documents where necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public selected by the founders; CIRCE/PAE may coordinate eligible electronic formations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders or duly authorized representatives execute the notarized deed. The deed must identify the founders, contributions, shares, directors, registered office, corporate purpose, and approved articles. Foreign powers of attorney must satisfy Spanish form, legalization, and translation requirements. Obtain an authorized electronic or paper copy for filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Execute a corrective or supplementary deed if the notary identifies omissions or errors; re-execute where required and preserve the original filing sequence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the provisional company NIF and tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT), through its electronic office or the CIRCE/DUE process where available.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a provisional company NIF using Modelo 036 and the incorporation deed or equivalent notarial evidence. Complete tax census registration and state the intended activities and tax obligations. After Mercantile Registry registration, submit the registered deed and obtain or confirm the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: Description of activities and tax obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the AEAT channel specified in the notice, correct census or identity data, and provide the missing deed or authority documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mercantile Registry for the province of the registered office; electronic submission may be made by the notary or through an authorized filing channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed and required supporting documents for registration. Pay the applicable Registry tariff; registration is required for acquisition of full corporate legal personality as an SL. Monitor the filing status and collect the registered deed and registry details. Complete definitive-NIF formalities with AEAT.
required_dossiers: Proof of applicable Registry fee payment
Any required foreign-document translations or legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address the registrar’s written qualification within the stated cure period by filing corrected or supplemental documents, executing a corrective deed, or using the statutory appeal or renewed-presentation procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete commencement, beneficial-owner, and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT; Social Security General Treasury (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social); competent regional and municipal authorities; and the relevant beneficial-ownership information system or notarial channel as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the tax census update, retain the company’s mandatory corporate books, and verify beneficial-owner information reporting obligations. Register as an employer with Social Security and enroll employees before work begins. Obtain any required regional industrial-establishment registration and municipal activity, works, or environmental authorization before fitting out or operating the facility.
required_dossiers: Social Security employer registration and employee data, if applicable
Facility plans, activity description, and technical reports required by the relevant authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct filings with the authority that issued the notice, submit outstanding technical or ownership evidence, and do not commence regulated activity until required approvals or declarations are effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent industrial authority of the Autonomous Community where the plant is located, under Law 21/1992 on Industry and Royal Decree 559/2010 regulating the Integrated Industrial Register; the municipality and regional environmental authority separately administer premises and environmental controls.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No single nationwide manufacturing operating licence is prescribed solely for manufacture of marine outboard engines or compact generators. The facility may require a municipal activity or environmental authorization/declaration and registration or notification as an industrial establishment with the competent Autonomous Community, depending on location, processes, and applicable regional rules.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The environmental authority designated by the Autonomous Community in which the project is located; the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico) is the state authority where state competence applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not automatically subject to a full EIA solely because of the stated manufacturing activity. The authority must screen the specific site, capacity, processes, and associated infrastructure under Law 21/2013 and applicable regional law; projects listed in Annex I require ordinary assessment, and Annex II projects may require simplified assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single sector-wide numerical threshold can be determined from the stated activity alone. Obtain applicable discharge authorization and comply with permit-specific wastewater limits, receiving-system conditions, and municipal sewer rules. Air emissions, including VOCs and combustion emissions, are subject to applicable regional air-quality permits and national implementing rules. Hazardous and non-hazardous wastes must be classified, stored, documented, and transferred through authorized operators under Law 7/2022; permit conditions and process-specific rules control.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operation, verify building and occupancy requirements with the municipality, including applicable fire-protection design and inspection requirements under Royal Decree 2267/2004 for industrial establishments and the Technical Building Code. Obtain required fire-safety documentation or inspection acceptance from the competent regional or municipal authority. Structural design and floor loading must be certified for machinery and storage loads. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention and implementing regulations, including risk assessment, preventive planning, machine safety, employee training, and workplace conditions. Additional regional inspections or certificates may apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); tax procedures are administered through the AEAT Sede Electrónica. Regional tax authorities have competence over certain indirect taxes in the Basque Country and Navarre; ordinary Spanish VAT applies elsewhere.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF during incorporation and a definitive NIF after registration and filing the required information with the AEAT, generally using Modelo 036. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment applies for a Spanish NIF through Modelo 036 and provides evidence of its legal existence, constitutional documents, representation authority, and the identity and tax details of its representative; documents may require apostille or legalization and sworn translation. A non-EU entity may need to appoint a Spanish fiscal representative where required by Spanish law or an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement. A business making intra-Community supplies or acquisitions applies for registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) through Modelo 036; its VAT number is then verified through VIES. Taxable businesses must register before commencing relevant taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no US-style check-the-box election for an SL. An SL is generally subject to Spanish corporate income tax as a separate legal person. Eligible corporate groups may elect the corporate tax consolidation regime by meeting statutory conditions and filing the required election. Other elections and special regimes may apply to qualifying transactions or activities; these do not generally change the SL's default classification. Spanish hybrid-mismatch rules may deny deductions or require income inclusion in specified cases but do not provide a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold applies to VAT registration for a person carrying out taxable economic activity. A non-established taxable person generally must register before making taxable supplies for which it is liable to account for Spanish VAT; the limited EU small-business threshold rules do not create a general threshold for foreign businesses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not generally require real-time pre-clearance of every domestic VAT invoice. The SII electronic VAT reporting system applies to specified taxpayers, including large businesses exceeding the statutory turnover threshold, entities registered for monthly VAT refunds, and members of VAT groups; covered taxpayers transmit invoice-register data electronically within the applicable statutory period, generally four days subject to legal exceptions. B2G invoices must generally be electronic and submitted through the public-sector channel, including FACe where applicable. Law 18/2022 provides for phased mandatory B2B electronic invoicing, subject to implementing regulations and transition periods. The AEAT Veri*Factu invoicing-system requirements apply according to their statutory scope and implementation timetable; taxpayers must verify current commencement dates and applicable exceptions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the EU may qualify for the VAT exemption with a right to deduct, subject to the statutory conditions and proof of export. The supplier must retain evidence that the goods actually left the EU and evidence linking the export to the supply. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: treatment depends on place-of-supply rules, customer status, service type, and any applicable exemption. A service supplied to a non-EU customer may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT rather than a zero-rated export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and MRN, together with official confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and sales contract or purchase order identifying the goods, customer, and supply
Bill of lading, sea waybill, air waybill, CMR, or other transport document, as applicable
Proof of delivery or other evidence of dispatch to a destination outside the EU
Accounting and payment records supporting the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a general statutory prerequisite for Spanish export zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain imposes no general statutory deadline for repatriating export proceeds. The taxpayer must substantiate the exemption and preserve supporting records. If eligibility or proof is insufficient, the AEAT may deny the exemption, assess VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties, and adjust related input-tax deductions. Tax penalties depend on the infringement and culpability; serious or very serious tax breaches can attract percentage-based penalties, commonly within statutory ranges of 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount. Fraudulent documentation may also trigger separate administrative or criminal consequences.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España; foreign exchange statistical reporting and formalities are coordinated with the Spanish General Secretariat of the Treasury and International Finance (Secretaría General del Tesoro y Financiación Internacional) under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, and anti-money-laundering supervision by SEPBLAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63-65). The Euro is legal tender and freely transferable within the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) and cross-border. There is no prior exchange-control authorization for capital contributions, dividends, repayments of shareholder loans, or profit remittances by an ES_SL. Operational constraints are limited to statistical declarations to the Banco de España through the banking channel, tax withholding formalities (19% on dividends/interest unless reduced by an EU directive or tax treaty), and the obligation to provide a Spanish resident address and NIE/Tax ID for resident agents. The capital account is fully open for non-resident shareholders of an ES_SL; no distinction is made between current and capital transactions for FX convertibility purposes, although transaction codes must accurately separate them for banking statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion of export proceeds since the full liberalization of capital movements confirmed in 1992. A Spanish exporter may leave foreign currency in an approved account with an authorized Spanish entity or choose to convert to EUR at market rates. Export proceeds must be settled through an authorized market participant (bank, savings bank, or registered EEA payment institution) when the transaction exceeds the reporting threshold set by Banco de España (commonly EUR 50,000 per operation or EUR 1,000,000 annual aggregates, as updated by Banco de España circulars). There is no fixed timeline for forced conversion; the exporter may hold receivables in the original invoicing currency, although annual CIT tax filings require detection of FX gains/losses under IAS/GAAP. All export collection must be supported by a commercial invoice, transport document, and customs exit authorization for VAT/Intrastat/ALTEX purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions authorized in another EEA state may provide SEPA payment services and e-money accounts in Spain without establishing a Spanish branch, using the 'passport' regime under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and Spanish Law 21/2011 on money electronic issuance. Feasibility for routine SWIFT/TT disbursements is High for EEA-licensed EMIs (e.g., Ireland and Lithuania), because they can issue IBANs in the local clearing area and process MT103 conversions through partner banks. Feasibility is Low for non-EEA digital EMIs (UK, U.S., APAC) because they lack SEPA clearing access and often cannot open a Spanish escrow account with proper dual control. EMIs are not viable for documentary commercial letters of credit or complex trade finance since they are not credit institutions and do not issue LC instruments under UCP600. For capital escrow/repatriation, a full banking relationship with a Spanish credit institution is legally safer and operationally necessary.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The ES_SL is a Spanish limited liability company and does not need a physical commercial office for bank onboarding; a Spanish registered address and recognized domiciliation service is sufficient. The Prevention of Money Laundering Act (Law 10/2010) and its implementing regulations allow non-face-to-face identification via video-identification procedures for natural person directors, but in practice the big Spanish financial institutions require a physical identity check at a Spanish branch, subsidiary office, or at a Spanish consulate/embassy abroad for non-resident directors and beneficial owners. The physical interview mandate varies by bank and by the risk classification of the jurisdiction; an EEA-resident director is often able to complete remote onboarding with authenticated electronic signature. Non-EEA directors or UBOs from high-risk third countries (e.g., China, Russia, LATAM) are subject to enhanced due diligence requiring a physical or notarized appearance. The recommended legal posture is to designate a Spanish-resident director/manager who can attend in-person for the initial account opening and thereafter accept board resolution copies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or opaque ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) in the Registro de Titularidad Real under Spanish company registry rules
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Escritura de Constitución, updated Registro Mercantil full company report, Form 604 declaration of UBO under Law 10/2010, notarized and legalized passports of all shareholders above 25%, NIE/Tax ID for each director, signed organizational chart demonstrating no nominee layers, and a law-firm certificate confirming the lawfulness of the ES_SL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reference in SWIFT MT103 Field 70 or supporting invoice to digital assets, cryptocurrency brokers, or FX conversion platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds declaration signed by the beneficial owner, audited/reviewed financial statements of the intermediate holding company, three most recent third-party bank statements, official invoice from the manufacture of outboard marine engines, and a formal written declaration that no cryptocurrency or unregulated digital asset channels have been or will be used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments routed to/from countries on FATF/EU high-risk or sanctions monitoring lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SEPBLAC-compliant transaction rationale, commercial contract with ISO Incoterms clauses, EORI number certificate, customs exit summary declaration for the physical shipment, dual-use/national security screening confirmation (or an official waiver), and copies of effective internal sanctions-screening policies covering EU/OFSI/OFAC ownership lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance and connection between declared trade activity and bank inflows/outflows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Closing balance sheet, projected cash flow and forecast for ISIC 2811 revenues from marine outboard engines, purchase orders from dealers/distributors, supplier contracts for LRM diesel engine components, warehouse lease or logistics service agreement, and VAT/CIT filing confirmation evidencing the beginning of commercial substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant protocol for an equity injection into the ES_SL from a foreign investor is a cross-border SWIFT MT103 payment in EUR or foreign currency made by the investor's bank to the ES_SL's Spanish IBAN. The payment must be sent to the designated capital escrow or operational account with Field 57D/59 containing the full IBAN and the ES_SL's registered name. For EUR-denominated capital movements, the principal clearing rail is SEPA Target2 / SEPA Credit Transfer. For non-EUR funding in USD/CNY, the executing Spanish bank will receive via SWIFT and convert using the interbank market rate; the conversion itself requires no prior authorization because Spain does not restrict capital imports. The Bank of Spain's balance-of-payments statistical regime requires the receiving Spanish bank to register the transaction under code E-1 (foreign capital investment) or similar, using the purpose descriptor 'cargo de fianza/constitución de garantía de capital' no; the correct payment purpose is 'aportación del socio para aumentos de capital / inversión extranjera directa' reporting. The ES_SL must comply with general foreign investment formalities: if the foreign investor is EU/EEA no prior clearance is needed; if non-EU and the target is active in sectors affecting public order/security, prior authorization under Law 19/2003 may apply, but a marine outboard engine manufacturer in ISIC 2811 is not within the default exceptional sectors; filing is an ex-post statistical obligation via the Foreign Investment Register (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores). For amounts exceeding EUR 250,000, the closing notary registration or shareholder resolution must clearly evidence the in-bound funding and the actual share allocation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Spanish engineering and component payments for marine outboard engine manufacturing will clear through three primary rails. SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR inside TARGET2/SEPA for European suppliers, using a standard IBAN-to-IBAN instruction with a mandatory UETR reference transmitted in the XML ISO 20022 pain.001. For non-EEA suppliers, the recommended rail is SWIFT MT103 over the SWIFT FIN network or SWIFT GPI, enriched with the ISO 20022 less code, bank charging convention, payment reference containing the invoice and PO number, and the 30-character information field shielded to commercial description only to avoid sanctions-triggering phrases. Trade settlements subject to documentary CDs are issued as an irrevocable documentary letter of credit under UCP600, instructed through Spain with MT700/MT710/MT707 messages, advised via the beneficiary's bank, and settled at sight by MT202 for reimbursements or MT754 for acceptances. If the company chooses open account trade settlement, use of a bank payment undertaking (BPU) or supply-chain finance facility is unnecessary but permissible. All disbursements above the Banco de España statistical threshold must be recoverable as the underlying commercial invoice, customs declaration, or transport document, supporting the bank's outgoing payment screening and preserving VAT/goods compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable outright forward contract with a Spanish bank for a notional amount strictly tied to the US-dollar-denominated export price for outboard engines, where physical delivery of USD and EUR occurs on the value date in the bank's nostro books.

EUR/CNY non-deliverable forward (NDF) for payments to Chinese component suppliers when a deliverable CNY market is inaccessible via the Spanish clearing infrastructure; the NDF is settled in EUR against the reference fix published by the offshore RMB market or the fixing determined at execution with a bank who can access the CNY fixed rate.

Cross-currency swap (FX swap) for short-term rebalancing of EUR/USD working capital where the ES_SL has a receivable in USD and a payable in EUR within the same business cycle; the FX swap is invoiced as a combination of spot FX plus forward revert and must be supported by a signed ISDA or Spanish bank's master agreement.

Plain vanilla EUR/CNY or EUR/USD currency options (call/put strips) allowing the manufacturer to hedge a highly uncertain tender for new exports to Latin America, with premiums payable in EUR and underlying trade exposure evidenced at the option maturity.

Spot-Forward combination hedge for the operational account when the company chooses to convert export proceeds from Latin America to EUR every month; permitted as synthetic forward without leverage, subject to the bank's treasury product suitability assessment and EMIR reporting obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit, including the beneficial-ownership declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) for the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve within six months after financial year-end; deposit within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, ordinarily approve by 30 June and deposit by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit may result in fines of EUR 1,200–60,000, subject to statutory criteria and higher limits for companies with revenue above EUR 6 million. The Registry may close the company’s filing sheet after one year from the filing deadline, subject to exceptions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax period ends; for a calendar-year taxpayer, ordinarily 1–25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior tax-authority request generally attracts statutory surcharges of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, increasing to 15% after 12 months, with late-payment interest thereafter. Filing after a request may trigger tax penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An audit is generally required when, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds at least two of these limits: total assets EUR 2.85 million; annual net turnover EUR 5.7 million; average employees 50. Other statutory triggers may apply, including group or regulated-entity rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad); applicable Spanish accounting rules govern statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Include the beneficial-ownership declaration with the annual accounts deposit and report relevant changes through the applicable Registry channels. Keep ownership and control information current; there is no separate annual confirmation of share transfers apart from the applicable annual declaration and change-reporting duties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro registro de socios)
Register of Directors and corporate officers, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–1,200 annually; a Spanish SL is not generally required to appoint a registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–12,000 for a small company, depending on complexity and audit scope; no statutory audit fee applies when an audit is not required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate (Art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014, LIS); newly created SLs engaged in active commercial manufacturing may apply a 15% reduced rate for the first two tax periods.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday; preferential mechanisms: (i) 15% reduced rate for newly created SLs; (ii) R&D tax credit of 25%-42% and technological innovation credit of 12% (Art. 35 LIS); (iii) participation exemption for qualifying foreign dividends retained (Art. 21 LIS); (iv) enhanced tax depreciation for digitalisation and energy-transition assets; (v) 25% exemption for reinvested extraordinary profits under certain conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry) for tax losses generated from fiscal year 2014 onwards; pre-2014 losses remain under the former 18-year carryforward regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Modelo 200) - annual Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) return; filed electronically through the AEAT e-Office (Sede Electrónica, www.agenciatributaria.gob.es); quarterly prepayments filed via Form 202 (Modelo 202); annual related-party informative return via Form 232 (Modelo 232).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 200) plus three quarterly installment prepayments (Form 202) in April, October and December; Form 232 is an annual exhibit to the tax file.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 200: within 25 calendar days following the six-month post-year-end window (e.g., a 31-Dec fiscal year-end is due no later than 25-Jul of the following year). Form 202 prepayments: due 1-20 April, 1-20 October and 1-20 December. Form 232 is due together with Form 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Resultado contable del ejercicio (accounting profit/loss)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pre-tax accounting result computed under the Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC), reflecting manufacturing revenue from light diesel outboard engines, inventory cost of sales, logistics and warehousing costs in Spain.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrue all intercompany sales to Latin American group affiliates at arm's length; ensure revenue from Spanish warehouse drop-shipping is properly attributable to the permanent establishment of the SL rather than to the foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted for permanent and temporary differences (e.g., non-deductible fines, provision timing, exemption of qualifying dividends, elimination of intra-group gains on transferred engine lines).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the participation exemption under Art. 21 LIS only if the non-resident parent's country is not on the Spanish tax-haven/blacklist; support all adjustments with contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax liability computed by applying the 25% general rate (or 15% reduced rate for a new SL) to the taxable base, before foreign tax credits and incentive deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the reduced 15% rate is not denied under Art. 29.1 LIS anti-asset-stripping rules if the manufacturing activity was previously carried on by the non-resident parent; document Spanish operational decision-making.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 600 - Cuota diferencial (resulting tax payable or refundable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net liability after deducting tax credits, double-taxation relief, withheld taxes and the three Form 202 installment payments made during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a refund is claimed, retain the parent's tax-residence certificates (TRC) and the 19% WHT evidence on any dividend distributions; correct any undeclared distribution before submission.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without payment: progressive surcharge - 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12) and 20% (beyond 12 months) plus statutory late interest. Incorrect declarations causing tax deficiency: Art. 191/192 LGT penalty of 50%-150% of the shortfall. Non-prejudicial formal omissions: fixed EUR 200 penalty (EUR 100 per abbreviated form). Non-payment triggers enforcement surcharges of 5%, 10% or 20% and coercive seizure of assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident shareholder (Art. 25.1 TRLIRNR); 0% available for EU qualifying parents under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (≥5% participation for ≥12 months); applicable DTA rates commonly 0%-15% for non-EU shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must: (i) obtain and deliver a valid TRC (certificado de residencia fiscal) covering the date of payment; (ii) evidence the minimum holding period and ownership percentage required by the applicable DTA or Directive; (iii) submit the TRC to the Spanish paying entity before the distribution so that the reduced rate is applied at source; (iv) where excess WHT was withheld, apply for a refund through the AEAT using Form 210/216 within the statutory four-year window; and (v) file annual informative Form 296 with AEAT by 31 January following the calendar year of distribution. Comprehensive beneficial-ownership declarations must be retained to discharge solidary liability.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory IRNR rate: 19% on both royalties and interest paid to non-residents (Art. 25.2 TRLIRNR); EU Interest & Royalty Directive (2003/49/EC) eliminates WHT for qualifying EU associated companies (≥25% capital for at least 24 months); bilateral DTA rates usually 5%-15% for interest and 5%-10% for royalties depending on the counterparty; anti-abuse rules require economic substance and genuine beneficial ownership of the Spanish payer.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR - Local File mandatory when net turnover of the Spanish taxpayer exceeds EUR 10 million; Master File mandatory when consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 45 million; Country-by-Country Report applies at group consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750 million. All transactions with related parties must nonetheless be priced at arm's length and supported by contemporaneous evidence irrespective of thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply an industry-specific Economic Substance Regulation; substance is instead enforced through the general anti-abuse rule (Art. 15 LGT), the sham-transaction doctrine (Art. 13 LGT), CFC rules (Art. 100 LIS), interest limitation rule (Art. 16 LIS, 30% EBITDA cap), DAC6 disclosure obligations and the EU ATAD/Unshell Directive signals. A Spanish SL manufacturing marine outboard engines must demonstrate real personnel, physical premises, local board decisions, purchase and distribution functions; a letterbox entity issuing invoices for foreign parents invites requalification, denial of exemptions and penal sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales of light diesel outboard engines to Latin American distributors through undisclosed foreign accounts, issuing false export invoices, destroying production and inventory records, or failing to file Form 200 for more than 12 months while understating Spanish taxable income above EUR 120,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 1-5 years and a fine of two to six times the defrauded amount (Art. 305 Código Penal); aggravated penalty of 2-6 years imprisonment where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 600,000 or where controlled entities are used intentionally; administrative penalty of 50%-150% of the deficiency plus late interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are personally criminally liable; courts may impose provisional imprisonment, suspension of passports and travel bans, and preventive embargo of personal assets; under Art. 42 LGT the director is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax debt, surcharges and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SL exclusively as an invoicing or treasury conduit for the non-resident parent; absence of employees, Spanish premises or strategic decision-making in Spain; routing back-to-back royalties, interest or dividends through low-tax jurisdictions with no operational reality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions under Art. 15 LGT and Art. 13 LGT, denial of deductions and of the Art. 21 participation exemption; penalty of 50%-150% of the resulting tax shortfall; CFC rules attributing passive income to the non-resident parent; potential commercial registry strike-off for failure to file annual accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly liable under Art. 43.1 LGT when they facilitated the artificial arrangement or dissolved the company leaving unpaid taxes; criminal money-laundering exposure if the shell moves proceeds; travel bans and asset freezing in criminal seizures; disqualification from managing companies for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling outboard engines to Latin American affiliates at margins departing from the arm's length standard; missing Local File, Master File or Form 232; unilateral and undocumented migration of R&D intangibles or brand royalties to an offshore related entity; back-to-back purchase/sale structures with no risk or function allocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compulsory tax adjustment adding the arm's length difference; formal documentation failures on Form 232 attract fixed fines of EUR 300-9,000; valuation adjustment for absence of contemporaneous documentation triggers a 15% penalty over the corrected amount (Art. 18.10 LIS); misrepresentation leading to a tax deficiency raises the penalty to 50%-150%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false intercompany documentation assume joint liability under Art. 42 LGT for the adjusted tax and surcharges; deliberately false valuations combined with evasion motive create criminal exposure under Art. 305 Código Penal; travel bans and personal embargoes may follow in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving repeated wire transfers (TT_Wire) or documentary credit payments (Swift_LC) from Latin American buyers without KYC/CDD reviews; accepting cash proceeds for marine engines above EUR 10,000; clearing corporate payments through the directors' personal accounts; failure to report unusual transactions to SEPBLAC or to file Form S-1 declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanction under Law 10/2010: very serious infringement fines of EUR 150,000-5,000,000, business closure or licence revocation; criminal money laundering under Art. 301 Código Penal: imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years plus a fine up to three times the laundered value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are natural persons criminally liable for money-laundering acts; passport surrender and travel ban; personal asset seizure; professional disqualification from managing companies; administrative fines also fall personally on the director who omitted AML internal controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Negligence on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident parent without applying the 19% statutory WHT; claiming treaty or Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption without a valid TRC or without satisfying the holding-period and beneficial-ownership tests; restructuring shareholder loans into equity to avoid withholding; paying royalties to foreign licensors without 19% IRNR.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish SL as withholding agent is jointly and severally liable for the unwithheld 19% plus late interest (Arts. 23.3 TRLIRNR and 41 LGT); penalty of 50%-150% on the omission; omission of Form 296 attracts a fixed fine of EUR 300-9,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who authorized the distribution without withholding is jointly and severally accountable for the entire debt under Art. 42.1(c) LGT; if the omitted withholding exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal referral under Art. 305 is mandatory; travel bans and cautionary embargoes may be ordered by the tax court.
